newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope says everyone has the right to a holiday.
newsitem.headline: Pope says everyone has the right to a holiday.

text.p: Pope John Paul added a new item to the list of human rights on Sunday -- the right to take a holiday.
Just days before he himself heads off for a short summer break to the Italian Alps, the Pope said everyone needed to get away from work once in a while.
"Every so often we all need a period of prolonged physical, psychological and spiritual rest," the Pope told pilgrims in St Peter's Square during his Sunday Angelus address.
"Especially for those who live in big cities, it is important to immerse yourself for some time in nature," he added.

But the Pontiff warned people against frittering away their vacations. "I would like to suggest, particularly to young people, to have healthy holidays...avoiding transgressions that are harmful to the health of them and others."
And the Pope added that "the right to holiday" should not make people forget those who cannot get away. "In the summer period certain public services are more important than ever," he told the crowd.
Pope John Paul is due to go to the Valle d'Aosta mountain region of northern Italy on July 9 for a 10-day holiday.
